resources.string: Found it at a new address, %1$s
Open WinDock on your computer, then pick it here.
Tap one to open its dock. Each computer keeps its own apps.
Don’t see your computer? Check that WinDock is running on it and that both are on the same Wi-Fi.
Make sure WinDock is running on your computer and both devices are on the same Wi-Fi. Guest networks often keep devices from seeing each other.
Security code changed. Tap to check.
Only this phone uses this name. Leave it empty to use %1$s.
To connect again, you’ll check the security code and enter a new PIN. Your dock stays on %1$s.
This phone will also be removed from %1$s.
%1$s isn’t reachable right now, so it will still list this phone until you remove it there.
On %1$s, click the WinDock icon in the taskbar tray, by the clock, and choose Show connection info.
On the Mac, open Terminal in the WinDock folder and run npm run info.
If the codes are different, another device on this network may be answering for %1$s. Check that you picked the right computer, then try again.
It’s on the same screen as the security code.
That PIN didn’t work. Check the 6 digits on %1$s and try again.
Too many tries from this phone. Try again in %1$s.
Couldn’t reach %1$s. Check that WinDock is running, then try again.
Choose Show connection info from the WinDock tray icon. That opens pairing for 10 minutes, and this screen continues by itself.
Run npm run info on the Mac. That opens pairing for 10 minutes, and this screen continues by itself.
Too many wrong PINs, so %1$s closed pairing.
The address is in Show connection info (Windows tray) or npm run info (Mac). The port is usually 8620.
WinDock only connects to computers on your local network, like 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x.
No WinDock answered at %1$s. Check the address and that WinDock is running.
WinDock keeps trying while this screen is open and opens the dock as soon as %1$s answers.
This phone is on a different network
This phone is at %1$s, but %2$s was at %3$s. Join the same Wi-Fi as the computer.
Look for the WinDock icon in the taskbar tray, by the clock.
On the Mac, run npm run mac:status to check.
The network lets devices see each other
Guest, hotel and office Wi-Fi often keep devices apart.
If macOS asked about node, choose Allow. You can change it in System Settings → Network → Firewall.
WinDock reaches %1$s over your local network. Join the same Wi-Fi and it will connect by itself.
That’s expected if WinDock was reinstalled or reset on %1$s. If it wasn’t, another device may be pretending to be it. Don’t continue until you’ve checked.
To check, open Show connection info on %1$s. If it shows the new code, pair again.
Plug this phone into the Windows computer with a USB data cable.
Turn on USB tethering in Android settings, under Hotspot & tethering.
Tethering can share this phone’s mobile data with the computer. Turn off mobile data if you don’t want that.
No computer found over USB. Check the cable and that USB tethering is on.
Scan the code on your computer
On the computer, open WinDock and choose Pair a new phone. Scanning pairs in one step, even if this phone can’t find the computer.
On the computer, open WinDock and choose Pair a new phone.
Open the camera and point it at the code.
Tap the link that appears. WinDock opens and asks before it pairs.
Nothing appears? Turn on QR scanning in the camera’s settings, or use Google Lens.
This isn’t a WinDock pairing code
This code needs a newer WinDock app. Update the app, or pair with the PIN instead.
This phone will open its dock and can launch apps on it.
Only pair if you just scanned this code on your own computer’s screen.
Each code pairs one phone, and %1$s shows a new one now.
The new code and PIN are in WinDock on the computer, under Pair a new phone.
The code says it’s at %1$s, but nothing answered there or on this network. WinDock keeps trying.
%1$s may have a new address. Scan the code again; it always shows the current one.
The code you scanned still works once pairing opens again, so there’s nothing to type.
The code you scanned doesn’t match the one saved when this phone paired. That’s expected if WinDock was reinstalled or reset. If you scanned it on %1$s’s own screen, it’s safe to pair again.
Pair again with the new code
On %1$s, click the WinDock icon in the taskbar tray, by the clock, and choose Pair a new phone.
On the Mac, click the WinDock icon in the menu bar and choose Pair a new phone.
Click the WinDock icon in the taskbar tray and choose Pair a new phone. That opens pairing for 10 minutes, and this screen continues by itself.
Click the WinDock icon in the Mac’s menu bar and choose Pair a new phone. That opens pairing for 10 minutes, and this screen continues by itself.
Its icon should be in the Mac’s menu bar.
To check, open WinDock on %1$s and choose Pair a new phone. If it shows the new code, pair again.
Couldn’t open the dock. Try again, or choose another computer.
The dock took too long to load. Check that WinDock is still running on %1$s, then try again.
Display settings for this phone only. Your computer’s display is unchanged.
Lower brightness reduces display wear. The screen stays on while WinDock is open.
Open Android Settings to change this option.
